title: Phantom Blade Zero Easter Eggs - Returning Skills, Weapons And Names
description: The callbacks in Phantom Blade Zero that are actually evidenced: two class skills from the original game returning in 3D, returning characters as bosses, and a set of weapon names that are Order codenames rather than blade models.
keyword: phantom blade zero easter eggs, pbz references, phantom blade zero callbacks, shadow of the eraser morse code, phantom blade zero original game

facts.label: Returning skills
facts.value: Two showcased in the launch trailer: the finishing dive of the Shadow class and the fire vortex of the Blazing Blade class, from the earlier mobile entries

facts.label: Returning characters
facts.value: Changhong and Lei Dang appear as adversaries; Mu Xiaokui returns with her attendants Yu Yao and Tie Gui

facts.label: Weapon names that are people
facts.value: The community roster lists 黑伤, 紫冥, 令剑 and 玉音子佩剑 - which match Order codenames and owners in series references

facts.label: The studio's own motif
facts.value: Red threads appear in the franchise's earliest logo, before this game existed

facts.label: Confirmed prop reuse
facts.value: The physical lion head from the Lion Dance boss was exhibited as a development prop in October 2026

facts.label: Caveat
facts.value: This game is a reboot, so callbacks are references rather than continuity

sections.title: What Is Actually A Callback Here
sections.content:
Phantom Blade Zero is the third outing for the same creator's world: it follows the indie Rainblood games and the mobile 影之刃 entries, and its director has called this project a spiritual rebirth of that earlier work rather than a sequel. So the callbacks are real, and they are references, not continuity.

The honest version of this page is a short list. Everything below has a source; the long inventories of "hidden references" that appear on fan sites for unreleased games are usually pattern-matching, and this page will not add to them.

sections.title: Two Class Skills Come Back In 3D
sections.content:
The launch trailer of 21-22 October 2026 shows two attacks that players of the mobile original will recognise, described by Chinese coverage as a crow-diving finishing strike from the 绝影 (Shadow) class and a 火龙卷 (fire vortex) from the 炽刃 (Blazing Blade) class. Both were signature abilities of those classes' promoted forms in the earlier games; here they reappear as Soul's moves, rebuilt for a 3D combat system.

The same coverage frames them as the trailer's nostalgia payload for series veterans, which is why they matter more as references than as new mechanics: they do not tell you anything about how the shipped build balances them.

sections.title: Returning Faces, Now On The Other Side
sections.content:
Three callbacks in the trailer's combat reel are characters rather than moves:

  • Changhong (长鸿) - a veteran of the earlier games, shown here fighting Soul from horseback with a spear.
  • Lei Dang (雷当) - also returning, and the closing fight of the trailer's combat section.
  • Mu Xiaokui (沐小葵) with Yu Yao and Tie Gui (玉妖、铁鬼) - the Order's young mistress, shown in a new form fighting alongside the two attendants who raised her in the earlier stories.

The pairing is the point: in the original games those two attendants are defined as her guards and stand-ins, so seeing all three in one encounter is a deliberate callback to that relationship rather than an arbitrary party design. Their own pages carry the footage details: Mu Xiaokui's encounter, Changhong and Lei Dang, all listed on the boss list.

sections.title: Weapon Names That Are Actually People
sections.content:
The most interesting callback is not in the trailer but in the roster. The community weapon list includes entries whose names do not read like blades:

  • 黑伤, plus 长形黑伤 and 黑伤双刃 - in series references 黑伤 is Soul's own codename inside The Order, which would make this a weapon family named for him rather than three unrelated swords.
  • 紫冥 - the same source material gives this as Zuo Shang's codename, and the wiki files the blade among weapons it cannot yet classify.
  • 令剑 - in the earlier games this is the ceremonial command sword Mu Xiaokui fights with, reshaped by the Order's craftsmen.
  • 玉音子佩剑 - literally "the carried sword of Yuyinzi", naming an owner rather than a make.

Mark this clearly as inference. The wiki does not claim any of these names refer to characters, and S-GAME has published no weapon lore. What is verifiable is the collision: the same strings appear as Order codenames in series references and as weapon entries in a roster that was compiled from footage. If it holds, a weapon list becomes a cast list, which fits the studio's rule that you earn a foe's weapon by beating them. It gets promoted from inference to fact the moment somebody can read an in-game description.

sections.title: Motifs And Physical Props
sections.content:
• Red threads. The director's own explanation of the motif predates this game - the threads appear in the earliest logo of the franchise, and he describes them as unseen hands with everyone tied to the far ends. The concept is on the lore page.
  • The lion head. The physical prop built for the Lion Dance boss was exhibited in Beijing in October 2026 alongside Soul's blade and mask, so the boss's design exists as an object the team handled.
  • Organization wanted posters. The collector's box includes an ink-wash wanted-poster print, which is the setting's own paperwork as merch: see collector's edition.

sections.title: What Does Not Count As An Easter Egg
sections.content:
Worth stating, because unreleased-game wikis are full of this: a visual similarity to another game, a boss that "feels like" a reference, a number that matches a date, or a name that rhymes with something in the earlier games is not evidence. Nothing on this page depends on that kind of match.

Two specific claims circulating that this page refuses: that the game hides a playable class-change system like the mobile titles (no source), and that a given boss is "actually" a named character from an earlier entry (the trailer shows adversaries, and only the three named above are reported as returning by coverage).

sections.title: Sources
sections.content: Compiled 27 October 2026 from: the launch trailer (21-22 October 2026) as reported by 3DM and Gematsu, for the returning skills and adversaries; the 影之刃 WIKI on BWIKI (fan wiki, unaffiliated with S-GAME) for the weapon names; Baidu Baike and the series wiki for the codenames and attendants; and S-GAME's own showcase and collector's-edition announcements for the motifs and props. The one inference on this page is labelled as an inference in its own paragraph.
